title: Hardy–Weinberg as a named diploid null
dek: p², 2pq, q². Wikipedia diploid equilibrium. Bacterial GWAS does not get this null for free; human GWAS uses it as QC.
story: Hardy–Weinberg on Wikipedia is the diploid random-mating null: genotype frequencies p², 2pq, q². Human GWAS uses HWE p-values as QC (bad assays, relatedness, structure).
Mtb is haploid and clonal. Pasting HWE filters into a bacterial pipeline is a category error. This card exists so the encyclopedia diploid null does not wander into TB WGS QC uninvited.
Structure and inbreeding both break HWE in humans; that is why HWE QC can throw away real ancestry signal if you are not careful.
deepTitle: Null as QC, not as biology of Mtb
deep: Exact tests exist for small counts; χ² is the large-count costume.
Filter HWE in controls, not automatically in cases, if the trait affects viability — a human-GWAS footnote.
For Mtb, QC is coverage, mapping, mixing, contamination — different plates.
Do not call a haploid SNP frequency a Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium.
